1.overview: John presents the Word as God, creator, life, and light, who becomes flesh as Jesus Christ and makes the Father known; John the Baptist testifies that Jesus is the Son of God and the Lamb of God. John identifies himself as the voice preparing the Lord’s way, while Jesus gathers Andrew, Simon Peter, Philip, and Nathanael, who recognize him as Messiah, Son of God, and King of Israel.

2.overview: At a wedding in Cana, Jesus turns water into wine as his first sign, revealing his glory to his disciples. In Jerusalem, he drives the sellers and money changers from the temple, speaks of raising the temple of his body, and remains wary of the people who believe because of his signs.

sections.heading: Jesus Knows What Is in People

3.overview: Nicodemus visits Jesus at night, and Jesus teaches that entry into God’s kingdom requires birth by the Spirit, then explains the Son of Man’s mission and the verdict on belief and unbelief. Jesus and John baptize in the Judean countryside, where John tells his disciples that he is not the Christ and that the Son from heaven must increase, concluding with the contrast between eternal life and God’s wrath.

sections.heading: Jesus teaches Nicodemus about new birth
The Son of Man and the verdict of belief
John explains his role beside Jesus
The Son from heaven and eternal life

4.overview: Jesus leaves Judea for Galilee, speaks with a Samaritan woman at Jacob’s well about living water and true worship, and many Samaritans believe that he is the Savior of the world. In Cana, Jesus heals a royal official’s son from a distance, and the official and his household believe.

sections.heading: The royal official’s son is healed

5.overview: At the pool of Bethesda in Jerusalem, Jesus heals a man who has been disabled for thirty-eight years, and the Sabbath healing leads the Jewish authorities to challenge him. Jesus explains his unity with the Father and his authority to give life and judge, then cites John, his works, the Father, Scripture, and Moses as witnesses to his identity and the authorities’ unbelief.

sections.heading: The Son’s Authority from the Father

6.overview: Jesus feeds five thousand people near the Sea of Galilee, walks across the sea to his disciples, and teaches in Capernaum that he is the bread of life who gives eternal life. Many disciples turn away over his teaching, while Peter affirms the Twelve’s belief, and Jesus identifies Judas as the one who will betray him.

sections.heading: Jesus Teaches About the Bread of Life

7.overview: Jesus goes secretly to the Feast of Tabernacles, teaches in the temple courts, and declares that his teaching comes from the Father who sent him as conflict grows over his identity and authority. On the feast’s final day, he offers living water, identified with the Spirit, and the crowd divides over whether he is the Prophet or the Christ while the authorities fail to arrest him and Nicodemus calls for a hearing under the law.

sections.heading: Jesus and His Brothers at the Feast
Debate over Jesus’ Origin and Mission
Living Water and Division over Jesus

8.overview: Jesus faces a test from the scribes and Pharisees over a woman caught in adultery, then declares himself the light of the world and debates with his opponents about his testimony, origin, and relationship to the Father. He tells those who believe him that his word brings freedom from sin, identifies his opponents’ father as the devil, and declares that he existed before Abraham; they try to stone him, but he leaves the temple area.

9.overview: Jesus heals a man born blind by sending him to wash in the Pool of Siloam, and the man’s neighbors and the Pharisees question him and his parents about the healing on the Sabbath. After the Pharisees reject his testimony and expel him, Jesus reveals himself to the man, who believes and worships him, while Jesus declares that he brings judgment between those who see and those who are blind.

sections.heading: Healing and the Man’s First Testimony
The Pharisees Question the Man and His Parents

10.overview: Jesus describes the sheepfold, identifies himself as the gate and the good shepherd, and says that he lays down his life and takes it up again; his words divide his hearers. At the Feast of Dedication in Jerusalem, Jesus speaks of his unity with the Father, answers accusations of blasphemy, escapes an attempt to seize him, and later receives belief from many across the Jordan.

sections.heading: The Gate and the Good Shepherd
Jesus at the Feast of Dedication

11.overview: Jesus delays going to Bethany, then raises Lazarus from the dead and declares himself the resurrection and the life. Many witnesses believe, while the chief priests and Pharisees plot to kill Jesus, who withdraws as Passover approaches.

12.overview: At Bethany, Mary anoints Jesus, while Judas objects and the chief priests plot against Lazarus; Jesus then enters Jerusalem to acclaim from the crowds. In response to Greek visitors, Jesus speaks of his death and glorification, and the chapter closes with the crowds’ unbelief, Isaiah’s words, and Jesus’ claims about his mission and the Father’s command.

13.overview: At the Passover meal, Jesus washes the disciples’ feet, explains the act as an example of service, and identifies Judas as the one who will betray him. After Judas leaves, Jesus speaks of his glorification and commands the disciples to love one another, then tells Peter that he will deny him three times.

14.overview: Jesus reassures the disciples of a place in the Father’s house, identifies himself as the way to the Father, and explains that his words and works reveal the Father. He promises the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, and peace to those who love and keep his word, then speaks of his departure and obedience to the Father.

sections.heading: A Place in the Father’s House

15.overview: Jesus presents himself as the true vine and the Father as the vineyard keeper, teaching that abiding in him produces fruit and that his disciples remain in his love through obedience and mutual love. He calls the disciples his friends and chosen witnesses, warns that the world will hate and persecute them as it hated him, and promises that the Spirit of truth will testify about him alongside them.

sections.heading: The Vine and Abiding in Love
The Spirit and the Disciples’ Testimony

16.overview: Jesus warns the disciples of persecution and explains that his departure brings the Advocate, who convicts the world and guides them in truth. He promises that their sorrow will turn to joy, speaks of asking the Father in his name, and tells the disciples they will scatter while he remains with the Father and has overcome the world.

17.overview: Jesus prays to the Father for the glorification that reflects their shared glory and for eternal life through knowing the Father and the Son. He asks the Father to protect and sanctify his disciples, then prays for future believers to be united in him so the world may know that the Father sent him.

sections.heading: Protection and sanctification for the disciples

18.overview: Jesus is arrested in a garden after identifying himself to Judas’s party and protecting his disciples, while Peter cuts off Malchus’s ear and later denies knowing Jesus three times. Annas and Caiaphas question Jesus, then Pilate interrogates him about his kingship and finds no basis for a charge, but the crowd demands Barabbas’s release.

19.overview: Pilate presents Jesus to the chief priests and the crowd, but under pressure he hands Him over for crucifixion. At Golgotha Jesus dies, fulfills Scripture, and is buried by Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus in a nearby tomb.

20.overview: Mary Magdalene finds Jesus’ tomb empty, and Peter and the other disciple inspect it; Jesus then appears to Mary and commissions her to tell the disciples. He appears to the disciples, gives them the Holy Spirit, and later meets Thomas, while the chapter concludes by stating that the recorded signs testify that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God.

21.overview: At the Sea of Tiberias, Jesus appears to seven disciples, directs them to a large catch of fish, and shares breakfast with them. He charges Peter to care for his followers, foretells Peter’s death, clarifies that the beloved disciple’s fate is not Peter’s concern, and the chapter closes with testimony to Jesus and a note on the many things he did.

sections.heading: The Catch and Breakfast by the Sea
Jesus Charges Peter to Shepherd His Sheep
The Disciple’s Testimony and Closing Note
